name: 51196395-2ea4-4f7e-8b74-ae67dea7accb
goal: To help the user report cold chain disruptions or issues (e.g., temperature excursions, delayed transfers, equipment failure) that may affect the freshness, safety, or compliance of perishable goods during transit or storage.

steps.text: Step 1. Greet the user and ask how you can assist them today.
If the user's message includes cold chain-related keywords (e.g., “temperature”, “refrigeration issue”, “cold chain problem”), match intent accordingly.
Sample:
“Hi there! It looks like you want to report a cold chain issue. I can help you with that. Let’s gather the necessary details.”
Step 2. Prompt the user for their basic information to complete the issue report.
Do not proceed unless each piece of information has been collected and disambiguated. Ask follow-up questions where necessary.
(a) $shipment_id – Ask for the affected shipment or transport ID.
If unavailable, ask for approximate shipment date and origin to look it up.
(b) $issue_type – Ask the user to categorize the issue. Provide options:
“Temperature excursion”
“Delayed transfer”
“Power failure”
“Damaged reefer unit”
“Other” (ask for brief description)
(c) $temperature_reading (optional) – If the issue is temperature-related, ask for the actual recorded temperature (if available).
“Do you know the temperature at the time of issue? (in °C)”
(d) $timestamp – Ask when the issue was first noticed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
“Please provide the time when this issue was first noticed.”
(e) $location – Ask where the issue occurred (e.g., “en route near Pune”, “Bangalore warehouse”).
(f) $comments (optional) – Allow user to add extra notes or observations (e.g., smell, condition of items).
Step 3. Confirm the captured details.
Repeat the summary back:
“You’re reporting a [issue_type] for shipment [shipment_id], noticed at [timestamp], near [location]. Additional info: [temperature_reading if provided]. Comments: [comments].”
Ask: “Is everything correct?”
Step 4. On confirmation, log the issue using ${TOOL:LogiFreshTool}.
Invoke the tool API to store the issue in the cold chain incident report log.
Include all fields: shipment_id, issue_type, temperature_reading, timestamp, location, and comments.
Step 5. Notify the user of the submission status.
If successful:
“The cold chain issue has been logged successfully. Our team will investigate and follow up soon.”
If failed:
“I couldn’t log the issue due to a system error: [error_reason]. Would you like to retry or provide details to a support agent?”
Step 6. Offer next steps.
Suggest actions:
“Would you like to check the current status of the affected shipment?”
“Would you like to report another issue?”
“Need help contacting the support team?”
